name: Banana peel teeth whitening
lead: Banana peel teeth whitening is a home practice in which the inside of a banana peel is rubbed on the teeth, usually for a few minutes a day, in the hope of making them look whiter. It is shared as a low-cost, natural alternative to peroxide whitening and is discussed in appearance and oral-care circles as a folk remedy.

Professional and over-the-counter whitening, by contrast, relies mainly on peroxide compounds that break down pigment molecules [1]. Encyclopedic sources describing banana peel composition and tooth whitening do not list teeth-whitening as a use of the peel [3], and no published clinical studies of the practice were found.
infobox: Typically the cost of a banana

paras: Practitioners describe rubbing the white inner side of a ripe banana peel against the teeth. Proponents attribute the effect to minerals or other compounds in the peel, though no published laboratory or clinical work was found testing these explanations. The peel is a protective outer layer of the fruit that is usually discarded after the fruit is eaten [3].

No studies found. Studies of tooth whitening more broadly concern peroxide-based products, whose results and side effects are documented (for example, tooth sensitivity is the most common side effect) [1].

Dental sources describe stains as intrinsic (inside the tooth) or extrinsic (on the surface), with peroxide agents aimed mainly at intrinsic stains and professional cleaning at surface stains [1]. Dental erosion, an irreversible loss of tooth structure from non-bacterial acids, is associated with acidic foods and drinks, and with frequent exposure [2]. Banana peel is not described in the sources reviewed as an acidic agent, and no reports of harm specific to the practice were found. Hygiene and pesticide residue on peels are general food-handling topics not covered by the sources reviewed.
The practice appears in lists of cheap or natural teeth-whitening tricks. No community-sourced material was available for citation here.

card.summary: Rubbing banana peel on teeth is a folk whitening trick; no clinical studies of it were found.
card.note: No published studies found; standard peroxide whitening has its own documented side effects.

quick.overview:
Banana peel whitening means rubbing the inside of a banana peel on the teeth for a few minutes, in the hope of brightening them. It is passed around as a cheap, natural home remedy.

No published clinical studies of the practice were found, and encyclopedic descriptions of the banana do not list it among the peel's uses.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say compounds or minerals in the peel lift stains. No published research was found testing that explanation. Established whitening works mainly by peroxide breaking down pigment molecules.
quick.risks: No specific harms from the practice were found in the sources reviewed. Dentists generally note that tooth stains differ in type and that surface stains are usually handled by professional cleaning.
